lessons.title: Read mute and aspirated h in phrases
lessons.objective: Use elision before French mute h and keep the boundary before aspirated h in a hotel and market exchange.
lessons.focus: French h is not an English /h/ sound. Say l'hôtel and l'homme with elision, but le héros, le hall, and le haricot without elision. Aspirated h also blocks liaison in les héros and les haricots.

words.en: The hotel opens at eight o'clock.
The man waits in the lobby.
The hero is on the poster.
The beans are at the market.

reader.fr: À huit heures, un homme entre dans l'hôtel près du marché.
reader.en: At eight o'clock, a man enters the hotel near the market.

reader.fr: Dans le hall, il voit l'affiche d'un film avec un héros célèbre.
reader.en: In the lobby, he sees a film poster with a famous hero.

reader.fr: Puis il sort et demande où trouver des haricots pour le dîner.
reader.en: Then he goes out and asks where to find beans for dinner.

reader.fr: La vendeuse lui montre les haricots sur son étal.
reader.en: The vendor shows him the beans on her stall.

speaking.scene: Finding a hotel lobby and the nearby market
speaking.opening: Bonjour, l'homme attend-il dans le hall de l'hôtel ?
goals: Ask whether the man is waiting in the lobby.
Mention the hero on the film poster.
Ask where to find beans at the market.
speaking.closure: Merci, je vais au marché chercher des haricots.

see.prompt: Sort hôtel, homme, heure with mute h and héros, hall, haricot with aspirated h; read the articles aloud.

recall.prompt: Recall the French phrase for 'the hotel opens at eight o'clock' before revealing it.

hear.prompt: Listen for l'hôtel or le hall in the recorded phrase and identify the word boundary.

type.prompt: Type the French sentence for 'The man waits in the lobby.'

say.prompt: Tell the receptionist that the hero is on the poster.

write.prompt: Write two French sentences placing the man at the hotel and the beans at the market.

lessons.title: Hear u, ou, and silent u in qu
lessons.objective: Distinguish French /y/ in rue and tu from /u/ in roue and tout, then read qui and quatre without adding a vowel after /k/.
lessons.focus: The letter u is heard as /y/ in rue and tu; ou is /u/ in roue and tout. In ordinary qui and quatre, the written u belongs to qu and is not an extra vowel. Keep rue and roue distinct when giving directions.

words.fr: Tu vois la rue sur la carte ?
words.en: Do you see the street on the map?

words.fr: La roue du vélo est abîmée.

reader.fr: Tu regardes la rue sur la carte avant de partir à vélo.
reader.en: You look at the street on the map before leaving by bicycle.

reader.fr: Mais la roue du vélo est abîmée, alors tu appelles ton ami.
reader.en: But the bicycle wheel is damaged, so you call your friend.

reader.fr: Il demande : « Qui a une voiture avec quatre roues en bon état ? »
reader.en: He asks, 'Who has a car with four wheels in good condition?'

reader.fr: Une amie propose sa voiture et tout le monde peut partir.
reader.en: A friend offers her car and everyone can leave.

speaking.scene: Changing transport after a bicycle wheel is damaged
speaking.opening: La roue du vélo est abîmée dans cette rue.
goals: Name the street on the map.
Explain that the bicycle wheel is damaged.
Ask who has a car with four working wheels.
speaking.closure: Merci, tout est prêt pour partir.

see.prompt: Mark /y/ in rue and tu, /u/ in roue and tout, then identify the single /k/ onset in qui and quatre.

recall.prompt: Recall the French word for wheel before revealing it.

hear.prompt: Listen for rue or roue in the recorded transport sentence.

type.prompt: Type the French sentence for 'The bicycle wheel is damaged.'
type.answerRef: La roue du vélo est abîmée.

say.prompt: Ask your friend who has four wheels.

write.prompt: Write two French sentences about the street, the bicycle wheel, and who can help.
